context: Tests whether the agent can run the triage-reviews skill dry-run for PR 42: fetch the four review comments, classify each into one of the documented categories (security, correctness, error-handling, performance, design, testing, style, nit, praise, question), evaluate each against CLAUDE.md conventions and the actual code, and produce a summary report without performing any write action.

checklist.name: Report exists
checklist.description: triage-report.md exists in the working directory and contains a PR header naming PR #42 or 'Add payment processing endpoint'.

checklist.name: All comments covered
checklist.description: The report covers all four review comments (ids 101, 102, 103, 104), each with a file/line reference or id.

checklist.name: Security identified
checklist.description: Comment 101 (string-interpolated SQL) is classified as security (or correctness) and its decision is accept.

checklist.name: Naming rename rejected
checklist.description: Comment 102 (rename process_payment to processPayment) is classified as style or nit, and its decision is reject with a reason citing the project's snake_case convention or ruff rule N802.

checklist.name: Praise acknowledged
checklist.description: Comment 103 is classified as praise and acknowledged (e.g. thank the reviewer), not fabricated into a task.

checklist.name: Question answered or answered-acknowledged
checklist.description: Comment 104 is classified as question with an answer or a statement of uncertainty, based on the actual code (the name comes from request.args).

checklist.name: Classification grounded in code
checklist.description: The report references the actual code at the commented locations (e.g. the interpolated query string in src/handler.py) rather than only quoting the comment text.

checklist.name: Dry-run stop respected
checklist.description: No write actions were performed: gh-record.json is absent or still an empty JSON list.

checklist.name: Follow-up grouping noted for accepted items
checklist.description: Accepted critical items are presented with a concrete follow-up proposal (e.g. a fix task for the SQL injection), though none was created.
